blocks.text: Expose a search controller that accepts a cancellable SearchFn, a complete non-query scope, and measured debounce and cache policy. It returns live input, explicit status, current results, selection identity, and clear or retry commands.

Contract checks:
- SearchFn receives the complete SearchKey and AbortSignal.
- Scope includes locale, filters, sort, and permission identity.
- Status distinguishes idle, loading, refreshing, success, no-results, and error.
- Timer, generation, controller, and raw cache stay private.
- Clear and retry preserve predictable input and selection behavior.

blocks.title: Core interfaces
rows: The caller receives the complete search input and AbortSignal, so obsolete network work can be cancelled without exposing controller ownership to the view.
debounceMs controls when typing intent is accepted; explicit submission may bypass it.
"cacheTtlMs defines how long cached results are considered fresh. If a query is repeated within that window, we serve cached results instantly."
{ input, setInput, status, results, error, activeResultId, clear, retry }
The view can render every state and preserve keyboard selection without seeing request runtime.
Status distinguishes empty input, first load, background refresh, useful results, zero results, and failure.

blocks.title: Required public behavior
items: A way to update the query (setQuery) while keeping typing instant.
A status field and error string to distinguish loading/success/error.
A results array that always reflects the latest valid query.
A clear() helper to reset query + results in one call.
A retry() helper to re-run the last debounced search after an error.
Config for debounceMs, cacheTtlMs, and minQueryLength.

blocks.title: Controller-internal state
items: Timer handles or raw setTimeout references.
Internal request ids or the full internal cache map.
Low-level flags like isDebouncing that don’t map directly to UX decisions.
APIs that require the caller to manage their own request ordering.
APIs that change shape depending on which state you’re in.

steps.title: 1. Setup
steps.text: The component calls useSearch(searchFn, { locale, filters, sort, permissionScope }, measuredOptions) and binds the field to search.input and search.setInput.

steps.title: 2. Typing
steps.text: As the user types, setInput updates input immediately. The controller debounces accepted intent without delaying composition or field rendering.

steps.title: 3. Cache + async search
steps.text: When intent is accepted, the controller checks the exact complete key. A miss or stale entry starts SearchFn with AbortSignal and a private generation guard.

steps.title: 4. Response / error
steps.text: On success, the hook updates results, sets status = 'success', clears error, and writes to cache. On failure, it sets status = 'error', populates error, and exposes retry() so the UI can render a Retry button.

steps.title: 5. Clear
steps.text: Clear aborts obsolete work, empties input and visible state, resets selection, and returns to idle without exposing or necessarily deleting the bounded cache.

items.label: API style
items.helperText: One call wires in debouncing, caching, and state.

items.label: UI contract
items.helperText: Components only need query, setters, and status flags.

items.label: Strong signal
items.helperText: Callers never see timers, request ids, or cache internals.

blocks.title: Contract checkpoint
blocks.text: A good search API makes complex behavior (debounce, caching, stale-response handling) invisible to consumers. If another engineer can build a polished search box using just your hook’s signature and state fields, you’ve designed the interface well.

SearchFn receives the complete SearchKey and AbortSignal. A cancelled promise is not shown as an error. Every success passes the active generation and key check before cache or UI commit. Result identities and accessible labels are stable enough to preserve keyboard selection across a background refresh.

steps.title: Accept intent
steps.text: Debounce incomplete text but react immediately to explicit filter submission.

steps.title: Check cache
steps.text: Read only the exact full key; optionally show stale data while revalidating.

steps.title: Cancel and call
steps.text: Abort obsolete work, create the next generation, and start the service.

steps.title: Publish
steps.text: Commit results only when generation and key still match, then repair selection by result identity.
